chunks: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

He asked about buried treasure: how much is due on it? He said, "The khums." And about mines: how much is due on them? He said, "The khums." And about lead, brass, iron, and whatever is from the minerals: how much is due on them? He said, "It is taken from them just as it is taken from the mines of gold and silver."

key_terms.الذَّهَبِ: gold, cited as a standard mineral category
key_terms.الصُّفْرِ: brass or copper-alloy metal mentioned among minerals
key_terms.الْحَدِيدِ: iron as a mined mineral resource
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth tax legally due on certain forms of wealth
key_terms.الْفِضَّةِ: silver, cited as a standard mineral category
key_terms.الْكَنْزِ: buried treasure or hoarded wealth discovered in the ground
key_terms.الْمَعَادِنِ: minerals or mines extracted from the earth

ai.seo_question: How much khums is due on buried treasure and extracted minerals in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that khums is due on buried treasure and on minerals extracted from the earth. It also clarifies that substances such as lead, brass, and iron are treated in the same way as gold and silver mines regarding this obligation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1645 - Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi asked Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about buried treasure: "How much is due on it?"

Imam (as) replied: "The Khums (one-fifth)."
He then asked about mines: "How much is due on them?"
Imam (as) replied: "The Khums."
He further asked about lead, brass, iron, and other mineral types: "How much is due on them?"
The Imam (as) replied: "The same is taken from them as is taken from mines of gold and silver."
